lesson_title: The Donation List: Paper One Essentials
hook_text: Five ways students donate marks to the marker — and the one-line habit that stops all five.
clip_script: Markers speak of donations: marks the script gives away that the mathematics never required. Donation one: rounding too early — the square root of eighty-four gets rounded on line two, and by the final line the answer misses the target. Donation two: the unchecked surd answer — squaring an equation invents candidates, and one of them usually fails the original. Donation three: the missing second answer — quadratics have two roots; simultaneous systems have two pairs. Donation four: finance without a timeline. Donation five: the limit written once and then abandoned. The habit that collects them all: after every answer, one check that costs a line. Substitute back, multiply back, count again. The paper rewards accuracy it can see.
visual_style: A hand slides coins across a desk toward a marker's red pen, one coin per donation; the final scene slams a one-line 'CHECK' stamp down and the coins slide back.
mood: Wry and corrective — the marks were always yours to keep.
pacing: Five quick coin-slides with a beat each, then a slow satisfying reversal on the check habit.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision sweep and stop donating marks.
